method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, proposition-by-proposition reverse paraphrase, exact formula, macro, token and identifier comparison; no independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Provability and consistency consequences for the LK sequent calculus: finite-cut preservation, the negation characterization of derivability, an explicit inconsistency proposition, and the exhaustive two-extension proposition.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section concerns the derivability relation and consistency. Its properties are individually significant and will be used in the completeness proof.
samples.checks: The heading, derivability token, consistency term and completeness-theorem role are preserved without adding a semantic claim.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If Gamma derives A and Gamma together with A is inconsistent, finite witnesses for the two derivations can be cut together; because both finite sets lie inside Gamma, Gamma is inconsistent.
samples.checks: The proposition condition, finite subsets, two derivations, cut tree and final subset argument remain exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma derives A exactly when Gamma together with not-A is inconsistent. One direction adds a left negation rule; the reverse direction cuts the derivation of not-A against the initial A sequent. The following exercise gives the dual statement for deriving not-A.
samples.checks: The biconditional, negation placement, both proof trees and the exercise instruction are preserved; the exercise is not silently solved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If Gamma derives A while not-A belongs to Gamma, a derivation of a finite Gamma-zero subset can be cut with the initial A sequent and exchange steps to derive the empty succedent, so Gamma is inconsistent.
samples.checks: The membership condition, derivability token, exchange and cut labels, sequent order and finite-subset conclusion are exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If both Gamma with A and Gamma with not-A are inconsistent, finite derivations yield a derivation of not-A from Gamma-zero and a derivation of the empty succedent from not-A and Gamma-one; cutting them proves Gamma inconsistent.
samples.checks: Both extensions, finite witnesses, the right-negation step, the cut tree and the union-subset conclusion retain their original direction and scope.
